5 Matchups to Watch on Thursday Night Football 🏈

Ravens vs Jaguars 🐆 🐦‍⬛

1. Derrick Henry vs the Jaguars Rush Defense 🐦‍⬛

Anthony Campanile’s defense has been phenomenal against the run this year. Through seven games, the Jaguars’ rush defense ranks 1st in EPA allowed (−0.21), 1st in rush success rate (34.4%), and 1st in yards per carry allowed (3.39). Meanwhile, the Ravens’ rushing offense has been about league average, ranking 20th in EPA per rush and 11th in rushing success rate.With Lamar Jackson out, the Ravens’ rushing attack takes a massive hit, as defenses can focus on stopping Derrick Henry. The one thing working in the Ravens’ favor is that the Jaguars’ stud nose tackle, DaVon Hamilton, is out for the year. (The Jaguars are allowing 3.84 YPC with Hamilton off the field this year compared to 3.05 with him on.) So there are still avenues for success for Henry in this game. The Ravens should also get back their stud guard Vega Iovane, from injury. 

As far as rush concepts go, the Jaguars have been dominant against zone concepts this year, allowing just 3.5 YPC and a 41.7% success rate against them. (62.7% of Derrick Henry’s rushing attempts this season have come on zone concepts.) Even with DaVon Hamilton out, the Jaguars’ defense should be able to contain Henry in this matchup.

2. The Ravens’ Pass Catchers vs the Jaguars’ Passing Defense 🐦‍⬛

From a coverage standpoint this season, the Jaguars have primarily operated in Cover 3/4/6 at a 65.9% rate.

Here’s how the Ravens’ pass catchers have matched up against Cover 3/4/6 this season:

Zay Flowers: 0.3 TPRR | 3.58 YPRR
Mark Andrews: 0.21 TPRR | 1.11 YPRR
Rashod Bateman: 0.15 TPRR | 1.74 YPRR
Devontez Walker: 0.09 TPRR | 0.96 YPRR
Jakobi Lane: 0.16 TPRR | 1.13 YPRR
Josh Cuevas: 0.27 TPRR | 2.3 YPRR
Justice Hill: 0.18 TPRR | 0.89 YPRR
Derrick Henry: 0.22 TPRR | 1.11 YPRR

It’s important to note that Joe Fagnano had just a 5.3 ADOT last week. Two Ravens pass catchers benefited the most from that: Mark Andrews had a 3.75 ADOT, and Justice Hill had a 0.43 ADOT. (Hill also had a 42.9% designed target percentage in Week 8.)

Meanwhile, Zay Flowers led the team in first-read share (26.7%) in Week 8. (Flowers also quietly owns an 8.03 ADOT this year against Cover 3/4/6.)

If I had to pick a Ravens pass catcher to go off in this matchup, it would be Zay Flowers, based on the designed work he’s likely to get and the fact that the Jaguars are allowing a 54.7% success rate through the slot this year.

The Jaguars’ passing defense ranks 20th in success rate (45.1%) this season, so there should be avenues for the Ravens to dink and dunk their way down the field.

3. The Jaguars’ Pass Catchers vs the Ravens’ Coverage Unit 🐆

From a coverage standpoint over the past month, the Ravens have primarily operated in Cover 2/3 at a 53.8% rate.

Here’s how the Jaguars’ pass catchers have matched up against Cover 2/3 this season:

Parker Washington: 0.22 TPRR | 2.11 YPRR
Brian Thomas Jr.: 0.09 TPRR | 0.23 YPRR
Brenton Strange: 0.37 TPRR | 3.58 YPRR
Nate Boerkircher: 0.08 TPRR | 0.86 YPRR
Bhayshul Tuten: 0.27 TPRR | 3.67 YPRR
Chris Rodriguez Jr.: 0.12 TPRR | 1 YPRR
Travis Hunter: 0.11 TPRR | 0.78 YPRR
Josh Cameron: 0.27 TPRR | 3.07 YPRR
Jakobi Meyers: 0.21 TPRR | 2.4 YPRR

Brenton Strange leads all Jaguars pass catchers in first-read share (25.2%) against Cover 2/3 this season. 

As for the Ravens’ coverage unit this season, they rank 19th in EPA per pass (0.01), 18th in success rate (44.6%), and 20th in yards per attempt allowed (7.41).

Nate Wiggins is questionable (illness). I’m 50/50 on him playing

If I had to pick a Jaguars pass catcher to thrive in this matchup, it would be Brenton Strange based on his success against Cover 2/3 this year.

4. The Jaguars’ Rushing Offense vs the Ravens’ Rushing Defense 🐆

With Bhayshul Tuten questionable and banged up, Chris Rodriguez Jr. is set to handle a bigger workload. C-Rod has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL this year, owning a 55.6% success rate and 0.2 MTF/A. He now faces a Ravens rush defense that’s been mediocre this season. Jesse Minter’s unit ranks 14th in EPA allowed (−0.1), 18th in success rate (42%), and 7th in yards per carry allowed (3.75).The one good thing for the Ravens’ defense in this matchup is that they’ve been dominant against man/gap concepts, allowing just 3.58 YPC with a 53.4% success rate against them this season. So I don’t see the Jaguars dominating time of possession with their run game unless if Tuten is 100% healthy.

5. Trevor Lawrence vs Jesse Minter’s Pressure Looks 🐆

The Ravens have pressured quarterbacks at the 8th-highest rate in the NFL over the past month (40.1% of dropbacks).

Trevor Lawrence has really struggled under pressure this season, posting a big-time throw to turnover-worthy play ratio of 2-to-8 and a completion rate of just 45.3%. With the Jaguars’ offensive line ranking 24th in pass-block win rate, I could see Lawrence struggling in this game against Minter’s simulated pressure looks.

Score Prediction

Ravens: 13
Jaguars: 24

If the Jaguars’ offensive line can keep Trevor Lawrence clean, they should be able to win by double digits. I don’t see many avenues for success for the Ravens’ offense, as Joe Fagnano doesn’t push the ball down the field. Also with Derrick Henry likely being neutralized, the Ravens will need a big-time game from Zay Flowers if they want any shot at an upset. Overall, I expect this game to be lower-scoring.
